omar: FYI: onboading gemma3b -> qwen-bridge conversion hit a weird generation drift only when we enable proj-transpose + int4-sym. small reproducer below.

omar: ```
prompt: Explain what a hash table is in simple terms.
ref (fp16 baseline): A hash table stores key-value pairs using a hash function to index values directly, making lookups fast.
converted+quant (proj-transpose on): Hash tables are arrays that keep keys and values together and are used for sorting.
```

omar: The converted model still matches logits at step 0 but diverges after ~16 tokens. not an immediate crash but meaning/precision drift. anyone seen proj transpose + rotary stride mismatches?

jess: which converter flags? also tokenizer? gemma3b uses bpe-v2?
omar: convert flags: `--to-qwen --proj-transpose --fused-softmax` ; quant: `sym-int4` per-tensor. tokenizer: gemma-bpe-v2 -> qwen-sp. we applied the tokenizer mapping script.

kevin: two quick suspects: 1) proj transpose changes how we split head dims vs proj dims (headstride mismatch). 2) tokenizer map might be dropping rare tokens -> eos position shift. which one shows earlier in trace?
omar: i diffed raw token ids and they're identical up to token 12. divergence starts after token 16. so tokenizer mapping probably fine.

bench-bot: quick metrics (converted gemma3b->qwen,int4-sym,proj-transpose):
- p50 gen latency: 96ms
- p95: 220ms
- mem: 7.2GB
- weirdness: KV head 5 magnitude ~30% lower after first 2 tokens compared to baseline

jess: can you dump rotary cos/sin tables and per-head KV for baseline vs converted? run `tools/kv_observe.py --model <path> --tokens 0:48 --out /tmp/kv/`

omar: did that. gist: https://internal.gists/4610/kv-observe (private). kv diff shows headwise amplitude scaling at head 5/11 and a phase offset ~0.78 rad (~pi/4) on a subset of heads.

kevin: pi/4 suggests a half-chunk/stride misalignment (we've seen pi/2 for swapped proj, pi/4 when half the dim is interpreted as positional subblock). if proj-transpose reorders the output vector layout, the rotary application indices can end up shifted by half-head-dim.

omar: quick hack: I patched runtime to skip proj-transpose (keep original proj layout) and re-ran quant -> generation aligns with fp16 baseline (diff negligible).

jess: good repro. sounds like converter should either re-lay out rotary tables to match the transposed proj OR avoid transposing when rotary present. which is easier?

kevin: adding a converter check is fastest: during convert check `if rotary_used and proj_transpose: emit warning + keep_layout` . longer term we should make runtime build rotary indices from meta describing post-transpose layout.

ci-bot: New CI job queued: converters/unit/rotary-index-check. will run on PR.

omar: filing a small PR with converter guard + a unit that builds cos/sin with transposed shapes and verifies per-head offsets. tagging @kevin @jess.

ops-bot: Staging pinned model: gemma3b-qwen-bridged:triage-4610 at 4610022238. No external routing.

jess: also note: when quant mode is sym-int4 we saw larger amplitude loss vs dq. maybe quant noise amplifies misaligned rotary effects. add a smoke test combining both axes: transpose x quant mode matrix.

kevin: agreed. I'll add a parameterized smoke test across {no-transpose, transpose} x {dq, sym-int4} x {headfuse on/off}. CI run will cover.

omar: thanks all. timeline? I want fix and hotpatch to dedicated pool today if possible.

kevin: PR in ~90m, CI ~1.5h, can hotpatch after green.

omar: perfect. leaving logs here and will follow up with gist links.
